decisive_items: Thin-walled, irregularly branched blood vessels dispersed between thickened collagen bundles
Endothelial cells were plump but displayed no significant cytologic atypia
response.rationale: The histopathology shows benign vascular proliferation with thin-walled vessels dissecting collagen, plump but non-atypical endothelial cells, and low proliferation index. Negative HHV-8 and D2-40 rule out Kaposi sarcoma and lymphatic origin. This is most consistent with hemangioma. ALHE would show prominent eosinophilic infiltrate, which is absent. AVM would have thick-walled vessels.

rejected.why: Arteriovenous malformation typically shows thick-walled arteries and veins, not thin-walled irregular vessels, and is usually congenital.
Angiolymphoid hyperplasia with eosinophilia requires an inflammatory infiltrate with eosinophils and lymphoid follicles, which are not described here.
